items.rationalization: An editorial of commendation, appreciation, or tribute praises, commends, or pays tribute to a person or organization that has performed some worthwhile projects or deeds, or accomplishments. Example: 'Laurels to Barangay Dance Troupe.'

mnemonic.title: Commend = Praise
mnemonic.phrase: EDITORIAL OF COMMENDATION = PRAISE + TRIBUTE

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial is oftentimes called editorial of persuasion, where the editor argues to convince or persuade the reader to accept his stand on the issue?
items.rationalization: An editorial of argumentation is oftentimes called editorial of persuasion. The editor argues in order to convince or persuade the reader to accept his stand on the issue. Example: 'Freedom of the Press Not Violated.'

mnemonic.title: Argue = Persuade
mnemonic.phrase: EDITORIAL OF ARGUMENTATION = PERSUASION + convince reader

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial evokes a smile, a chuckle, or laughter while suggesting truth, with its main aim to entertain?
items.rationalization: An editorial of entertainment evokes a smile, a chuckle, laughter, while suggesting truth. Its main aim is to entertain. It is usually short. Example: 'Miniskirt, Anyone?'

mnemonic.title: Entertain = Smile
mnemonic.phrase: EDITORIAL OF ENTERTAINMENT = SMILE + TRUTH + SHORT

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial presents a philosophy rather than an argument or explanation, often with nature or emotion as subject matter?
items.rationalization: A mood editorial presents a philosophy rather than an argument or an explanation. Oftentimes, the subject matter is nature or emotion. Example: 'Those Wonderful People Called Parents.'

mnemonic.title: Mood = Philosophy
mnemonic.phrase: MOOD EDITORIAL = PHILOSOPHY + nature/emotion

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial explains the significance of a special day or occasion?
items.rationalization: A special occasion editorial explains the significance of a special day or occasion. Examples: 'The Significance of Christmas,' 'Au Revoir.'
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is an editorial written by two or more editors belonging to different newspapers which they publish in their respective papers at the same time?
items.rationalization: A pooled editorial is written by two or more editors belonging to different newspapers which they publish in their respective papers at the same time. Example: 'Stop Tuition Fee Increase.'

mnemonic.title: Pooled = Shared
mnemonic.phrase: POOLED EDITORIAL = TWO+ editors + DIFFERENT papers + SAME time

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the three parts of an editorial?
items.rationalization: An editorial is organized in three parts: (1) the introduction, which contains the newspeg with the reaction and is usually one short paragraph; (2) the body, which may take two or three short paragraphs that support or justify the reaction; and (3) the ending, sometimes called the clincher, which summarizes the editorial's stand.

mnemonic.title: 3 Parts
mnemonic.phrase: I-B-E: Introduction, Body, Ending (clincher)

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the ending of an editorial, which summarizes the editorial's stand, sometimes called?
items.rationalization: The ending of an editorial, sometimes called the clincher, summarizes the editorial's stand. The body may take two or three short paragraphs that support or justify the reaction.

mnemonic.title: Clincher
mnemonic.phrase: CLINCHER = editorial ENDING that summarizes STAND

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial column resembles an editorial in form but carries the personal stamp of the writer's own ideas, also called the signed editorial column?
items.rationalization: The opinion column (also called the signed editorial column) resembles an editorial in form but, in contrast with the editorial's impersonal and anonymous approach, carries the personal stamp of the writer's own ideas. Example: Walter Lippman's 'Today and Tomorrow.'

mnemonic.title: Opinion = Personal
mnemonic.phrase: OPINION column = SIGNED + PERSONAL ideas

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial column lumps together odds and ends of information, a poem here, an announcement there, a joke, or an interesting quotation?
items.rationalization: The hodge-podge column is where the author lumps together odds and ends of information, a poem here, an announcement there, a point paragraph, a modernized proverb, a joke, or an interesting quotation. It is one of the types of editorial columns according to content.

mnemonic.title: Hodge-podge = Mix
mnemonic.phrase: HODGE-PODGE = MIX of odds and ends

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial column is a legacy from a more leisurely age, exemplified by Addison and Steele of the Spectator papers, Charles Lamb, Oliver Goldsmith, G.K. Chesterton, and Christopher Morley?
items.rationalization: The essay column (increasingly rare) is a legacy from a more leisurely age when writers could sit and scribble and muse in light or purple prose. Its exponents were Addison and Steele of the famed Spectator papers, Charles Lamb, Oliver Goldsmith, G.K. Chesterton, and Christopher Morley. The Filipino columnist who best approximated this type was Godofredo Rivera of the Graphic.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial column caters to the inherent interest of human beings in human beings, chronicling the facts and foibles of the great and near-great, exemplified by Walter Winchell?
items.rationalization: The gossip column caters to the inherent interest of human beings in human beings. Unfortunately, the reader's eyes light up more frequently when they spy the vices rather than the virtues of others. The society columnists chronicle the facts and foibles of the great and near-great, the social climbers, and the true celebrities. Example: Walter Winchell and his 'keyhole' journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of editorial column is written by a columnist who has his eye to the keyhole but with a more serious purpose, poking into the activities of the 'men who make the decisions'?
items.rationalization: The dopester's column is written by the columnist who also has his eye to the keyhole but with a more serious purpose. He uses much the same technique as the gossip columnist but rises above the chatterbox variety of news to poke into the activities of the 'men who make the decisions.' The 'victims' are usually government leader-politicians, congressmen, senators, Cabinet officials, titans of industry and commerce, and institutions which have to do with national and international affairs.

mnemonic.title: Dopester = Serious
mnemonic.phrase: DOPESTER = GOSSIP technique + SERIOUS purpose (decision-makers)

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is an editorial page illustration expressing opinion and interpretation, derived from the words caricature and lampoon?
items.rationalization: An editorial cartoon is an editorial page illustration expressing opinion and interpretation. The word cartoon is derived from two words: caricature and lampoon. It performs any of the three functions of the newspress – to inform, influence, or entertain.

mnemonic.title: Cartoon = Caricature + Lampoon
mnemonic.phrase: CARTOON = CARICATURE + LAMPOON

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is an exaggerated description, generally by sketching, a pictorial representation of a person or thing in which a defect or peculiarity is exaggerated so as to produce a ludicrous effect?
items.rationalization: A caricature is an exaggerated description, generally by sketching. It is a pictorial representation of a person or thing in which a defect or peculiarity is exaggerated so as to produce a ludicrous effect. Together with lampoon, it is one of the two words from which 'cartoon' is derived.

mnemonic.title: Caricature = Exaggerate
mnemonic.phrase: CARICATURE = EXAGGERATED sketch + LUDICROUS effect

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a piece of malicious writing, a personal written satire that attacks and ridicules?
items.rationalization: A lampoon is a piece of malicious writing, a personal written satire that attacks and ridicules. Together with caricature, it is one of the two words from which 'cartoon' is derived.

mnemonic.title: Lampoon = Attack
mnemonic.phrase: LAMPOON = MALICIOUS writing + ATTACK/RIDICULE

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the three functions of the newspress that an editorial cartoon also performs?
items.rationalization: An editorial cartoon performs any of the three functions of the newspress – to inform, influence, or entertain. A good cartoon appeals to the reader's sense of humor in order to persuade him to accept an opinion; it is an effective social force.

mnemonic.title: 3 Functions
mnemonic.phrase: I-I-E: Inform, Influence, Entertain

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of cartoon idea shows the school represented as a mother taking care of her children?
items.rationalization: An inspirational cartoon idea shows the school represented as a mother taking care of her children. Cartoon ideas cover a wide range of subjects: inspirational, satirical, and correctional.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of cartoon idea shows the embarrassment of having girls wear miniskirts in the classroom?
items.rationalization: A satirical cartoon idea shows the embarrassment of having girls wear miniskirts in the classroom. Cartoon ideas cover a wide range of subjects: inspirational, satirical, and correctional.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of cartoon idea shows problems involving people taking prohibited drugs?
items.rationalization: A correctional cartoon idea shows problems involving people taking prohibited drugs. Cartoon ideas cover a wide range of subjects: inspirational, satirical, and correctional.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a story based upon a news event that has already been covered by the newspaper, often called the story behind the story?
items.rationalization: A news feature is a story based upon a news event that has already been covered by the newspaper. It's the story behind the story. It is one of the types of feature articles.

mnemonic.title: News Feature
mnemonic.phrase: NEWS FEATURE = STORY BEHIND the story

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of feature analyzes the facts of a news story to explain the causes and motivations leading to the event, then discusses the possible consequences?
items.rationalization: An interpretative feature analyzes the facts of a news story to explain the causes and motivations leading to the event, then discusses the possible consequences. It is one of the types of feature articles.

mnemonic.title: Interpretative
mnemonic.phrase: INTERPRETATIVE feature = CAUSES + MOTIVATIONS + CONSEQUENCES

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of feature is a general category referring to any interesting story about a person, place, or event that has no news peg or timeliness associated with it?
items.rationalization: A straight feature is a general category referring to any interesting story about a person, place, or event that has no 'news peg' or timeliness associated with it. It is one of the types of feature articles.

mnemonic.title: Straight Feature
mnemonic.phrase: STRAIGHT feature = NO news peg + NO timeliness

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of feature makes the readers aware of the subject's personality by detailing the person's experiences, thoughts, mannerisms, and actions?
items.rationalization: A personality feature makes the readers aware of the subject's personality by detailing the person's experiences, thoughts, mannerisms, and actions. It is one of the types of feature articles.

mnemonic.title: Personality
mnemonic.phrase: PERSONALITY feature = EXPERIENCES + THOUGHTS + MANNERISMS + ACTIONS

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of feature is usually about a prominent individual or an authority on a particular subject or event, the information of which is obtained in an interview?
items.rationalization: An interview feature is usually about a prominent individual or an authority on a particular subject or event, the information of which is obtained in an interview. It is one of the types of feature articles.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of feature establishes a mood and provokes an emotional reaction in a reader, and can be humorous or sad, suspenseful or fast-paced?
items.rationalization: A human-interest feature establishes a mood and provokes an emotional reaction in a reader. It can be humorous or sad, suspenseful or fast-paced. It is one of the types of feature articles.

mnemonic.title: Human Interest
mnemonic.phrase: HUMAN-INTEREST = MOOD + EMOTIONAL reaction

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is also called an analysis piece, which adds meaning to current issues in the news by explaining them further?
items.rationalization: A backgrounder — also called an analysis piece — adds meaning to current issues in the news by explaining them further. It is one of the types of feature articles.

mnemonic.title: Backgrounder
mnemonic.phrase: BACKGROUNDER = ANALYSIS piece + adds MEANING

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a newspaper term for brief feature items, usually humorous, less than 100 words, beginning with a clever lead and building to a surprise ending?
items.rationalization: Brites is a newspaper term for brief feature items – usually humorous. Less than 100 words, they begin with a clever lead that grabs the reader's attention and go on to a brief, chronological description of an event that builds swiftly to a climax – usually a surprise ending – or to a catchy, summary thought. Example: Reader's Digest.

mnemonic.title: Brites
mnemonic.phrase: BRITES = BRIEF + HUMOROUS + <100 words + SURPRISE ending

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is an art of asking questions to obtain information, or technically, asking questions to obtain opinions, ideas, or special information on topics of interest to the general public from a prominent person or recognized authority?
items.rationalization: An interview is an art of asking questions to obtain information. Technically speaking, it is asking questions to obtain opinions, ideas, or special information on topics of interest to the general public from a prominent person or from a recognized authority.

mnemonic.title: Interview
mnemonic.phrase: INTERVIEW = ASK questions + OBTAIN info/opinion

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What kind of interview is conducted to obtain some information from a person responsible for a new idea?
items.rationalization: An informative interview is conducted to obtain some information from a person responsible for a new idea. It is one of the kinds of interviews, along with opinion interview and feature interview.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What kind of interview is conducted to obtain opinion?
items.rationalization: An opinion interview is conducted to obtain opinion. It is one of the kinds of interviews, along with informative interview and feature interview.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What kind of interview is a group interview of which there are two types: the 'inquiring reporter type' and the symposium type?
items.rationalization: A feature interview is the group interview of which there are two types: the 'inquiring reporter type' and the symposium type. It is one of the kinds of interviews.

mnemonic.title: Feature Interview
mnemonic.phrase: FEATURE interview = GROUP + inquiring reporter/symposium types

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: In conducting an interview, what should you do regarding 'off the record' comments?
items.rationalization: In conducting an interview, you should respect 'off the record' comments. This is one of the dos in conducting an interview, along with knowing your subject thoroughly, making an appointment, being courteous, and offering to show your write-up before publication.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: In writing the interview, what should you do with grammatical errors and awkward sentences made by the interviewee?
items.definition: Correct them unless they are necessary to reveal his personality, without changing the interviewee's meaning
items.rationalization: In writing the interview, you should correct all grammatical errors and awkward sentences made by the interviewee unless they are necessary to reveal his personality. In doing this, don't change the interviewee's meaning.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the five W's that appear in the sports lead?
items.definition: Who won? Against whom? By what score? Where? When?
items.rationalization: The classic 'Five W's' appear in the sports lead as: Who won? Against whom? By what score? Where? When? The sports lead is the attention-getter, the news in a nutshell.

mnemonic.title: Sports 5 W's
mnemonic.phrase: WHO won + AGAINST whom + SCORE + WHERE + WHEN

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the elements that a sports lead can dramatize aside from the five W's?
items.definition: The key play, the outstanding player, and analytical approach
items.rationalization: The sports lead can also dramatize other elements like the key play, the outstanding player, and analytical approach. The sports lead is the attention-getter, the news in a nutshell.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What should a reporter use to identify the story on the first page, including the name of the paper, story identifier, reporter, and date?
items.rationalization: In preparing the copy, the reporter should identify on the first page the story with a slugline – the name of the paper, words identifying the story like 'Fire' or 'Student election,' the reporter, and the date.

mnemonic.title: Slugline
mnemonic.phrase: SLUGLINE = PAPER + STORY + REPORTER + DATE

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What symbol or word is typed at the bottom of each page except the last to indicate the story continues?
items.rationalization: In preparing the copy, the reporter should type the word 'More' at the bottom of each page except the last, where he has to indicate the end of the story with a '30' or # mark.

mnemonic.title: More & 30
mnemonic.phrase: MORE at bottom (except last); 30 or # at END

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the term for the assembling of type, cuts, and/or ads on a page?
items.rationalization: Makeup refers to the assembling of type, cuts, and/or ads on a page. Type refers to the texts or fonts used, while cuts in letterpress terminology refer to photoengraving of any kind, including photos, illustrations, and boxes.

mnemonic.title: Makeup
mnemonic.phrase: MAKEUP = assembling TYPE + CUTS + ADS on a page

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a column of type extending down a page, not squared off under a multicolumn headline, that should be avoided in makeup?
items.rationalization: A dogleg refers to a column of type extending down a page, not squared off under a multicolumn headline. Avoiding clutter by avoiding doglegs is one of the dos and don'ts in makeup.

mnemonic.title: Dogleg
mnemonic.phrase: DOGLEG = column NOT squared off + AVOID

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the placement of a headline directly under a multicolumn head, which should be avoided in makeup?
items.rationalization: Armpit placement is a headline directly under a multicolumn head. It should be avoided in makeup to prevent clutter and poor visual arrangement.

mnemonic.title: Armpit
mnemonic.phrase: ARMPIT placement = headline UNDER multicolumn head + AVOID

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the six principles to achieve effective makeup according to Scholastic Journalism by English and Hach?
items.definition: Unity, balance, emphasis, movement, proportion, and contrast
items.rationalization: Scholastic Journalism by English and Hach gives six principles to achieve effective makeup: unity, balance, emphasis, movement, proportion, and contrast. These principles guide the arrangement of elements on a newspaper page.

mnemonic.title: UBEMPC
mnemonic.phrase: U-B-E-M-P-C: Unity, Balance, Emphasis, Movement, Proportion, Contrast

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the term for placing two headlines of the same size side by side, which should be avoided in makeup?
items.rationalization: Tombstoning refers to placing two headlines of the same size side by side. It should be avoided in page makeup because it creates visual confusion and monotony.

mnemonic.title: Tombstoning
mnemonic.phrase: TOMBSTONING = TWO same-size headlines SIDE BY SIDE + AVOID

items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of front page makeup is also called balance or symmetrical makeup?
items.rationalization: Perfect balance makeup is also called balance or symmetrical makeup. It is one of the types of front page makeup by way of headline and text arrangement identified by English and Hach in Scholastic Journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of front page makeup is also called brace or focus makeup?
items.rationalization: Brace or focus makeup is one of the types of front page makeup by way of headline and text arrangement. It is identified by English and Hach in Scholastic Journalism, along with perfect balance, broken column, occult, streamlined, and circus makeup.
items.tosCompetency: Apply principles and strategies in writing various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of front page makeup includes the X format, curve format, L format, J format, and umbrella format?
items.definition: Makeup by way of text and photo combination
items.rationalization: Makeup by way of text and photo combination includes the X format, curve format, L format, J format, and umbrella format. This is another way of laying out a page, distinct from makeup by way of headline and text arrangement.

mnemonic.title: XCLJU

items.term: What are the two things a newspaperman must bear in mind when selecting pictures for publication?
items.definition: The picture's technical value and editorial value
items.rationalization: The newspaperman has two things to bear in mind when selecting pictures for publication: the picture's technical value and editorial value. A picture has technical value when it is technically perfect with proper light and shadow, free from smudges, and clean and clear. A picture has editorial value when it tells a story at a glance and shows life's happenings and moments of truth and significance.

mnemonic.title: T-E Value
mnemonic.phrase: TECHNICAL value + EDITORIAL value

items.term: What is the text or body type accompanying photos or artwork, sometimes called cutline or underline?
items.rationalization: A caption is the text or body type accompanying photos or artwork or any pictorial illustration. It is sometimes called cutline or underline. The title or explanatory matter above an illustration is called an overline. Captions should be closely related to the picture so that the reader may be able to take in picture and caption at a glance.

mnemonic.title: Caption
mnemonic.phrase: CAPTION = CUTLINE = UNDERLINE (text below photo)

items.term: What is the title or explanatory matter above an illustration called?
items.rationalization: The title or explanatory matter above an illustration is called an overline. It is distinguished from the caption/cutline/underline, which is the text below the photo. Captions should be underneath the picture when there are other materials on the page, but can be on the side when picture and caption are isolated.

mnemonic.title: Overline
mnemonic.phrase: OVERLINE = text ABOVE photo

items.term: What presents rules that, when followed, lead to consistency in punctuation, abbreviation, capitalization, and spelling?
items.rationalization: A stylebook does not deal with matters of literary expression. It presents rules that, when followed, lead to consistency in punctuation, abbreviation, capitalization, and spelling. It is an essential reference for journalists.

items.term: According to Robert Gunning's Ten Principles of Clear Writing, what is the first principle?
items.definition: Keep sentences short, on the average
items.rationalization: According to Robert Gunning's Ten Principles of Clear Writing, the first principle is to keep sentences short, on the average. Sentences must vary in length if the reader is to be saved from boredom.

items.term: According to Robert Gunning, what should you prefer over the complex?
items.rationalization: According to Robert Gunning's Ten Principles of Clear Writing, you should prefer the simple to the complex. Zinsser wrote: 'The secret to good writing is to strip every sentence to its cleanest form.'

items.term: According to Robert Gunning, what should you put into your verbs?
items.rationalization: According to Robert Gunning's Ten Principles of Clear Writing, you should put action into your verbs and use the active voice. This makes writing more direct and vigorous.

items.term: According to Robert Gunning, what should you write to, not to impress?
items.definition: Write to express, not to impress
items.rationalization: According to Robert Gunning's Ten Principles of Clear Writing, the tenth principle is to write to express, not to impress. Inform readers, that's all. This summarizes the essence of clear writing.
